description: A composite figure in two parts. (a) Atomic maps: three rows of EPMA elemental maps, one row per alloy — AN750-T (top), AN800-T (middle), AN850-T (bottom) — each row showing five side-by-side colour maps labelled Fe, C, M (Mn), Al and Si, with a 3 μm scale bar at bottom right. Hot colours (red/yellow) mark enrichment and blue depletion; the C map of every row carries a red dashed vertical line ending in a downward arrow that defines the line-scan path used in (b). (b) Atomic concentration statistics: for each alloy, four vertically stacked profiles of Si content (at.%), Al content (at.%), Mn content (at.%) and C content (at.%) versus Distance (μm) over about 0–30 μm, drawn with error bars; light-grey vertical bands labelled B, TM, RA and FM mark the phase regions crossed by the line scan. In AN750-T the C profile shows marked maxima aligned with the B, RA and FM bands (reaching a few at.%), while Si, Al and Mn stay nearly flat; in AN800-T and AN850-T the C maxima are smaller and the profiles flatter. The figure demonstrates that raising the annealing temperature homogenises carbon between the B/TM, RA and FM phases while the other elements remain uniformly distributed: (a) locates the phases, (b) quantifies them.

subfigures.description: EPMA elemental maps arranged in three rows (AN750-T, AN800-T, AN850-T), each row with five maps labelled Fe, C, M (Mn), Al and Si; a 3 μm scale bar is present. A red dashed vertical line with a downward arrow is drawn on the C map of each row, marking the line-scan path. Colour scale runs blue (depleted) to red/yellow (enriched).

For each alloy (AN750-T, AN800-T, AN850-T) four stacked line profiles of Si content (at.%), Al content (at.%), Mn content (at.%) and C content (at.%) versus Distance (μm) (0–30 μm), with error bars and light-grey bands labelled B, TM, RA, FM marking the phase regions. Carbon shows the largest variability, peaking within the grey bands; Si, Al and Mn are comparatively flat.

observations.observation: Panel (a) shows EPMA elemental maps for Fe, C, M (Mn), Al and Si in three alloys labelled AN750-T, AN800-T and AN850-T.
Each row of maps in panel (a) carries a 3 μm scale bar.
The C map in each row of panel (a) is overlaid with a red dashed vertical line ending in a downward arrow, marking the line-scan path.
Panel (b) plots Si content, Al content, Mn content and C content (all in at.%) against Distance (μm) over roughly 0–30 μm, with error bars on every point.
Light-grey vertical bands labelled B, TM, RA and FM mark the phase regions crossed by the line scan in panel (b).
In the AN750-T profiles the C content curve shows pronounced maxima that coincide with the grey phase bands, whereas the Si, Al and Mn curves remain comparatively flat.
In AN800-T and AN850-T the C profiles show smaller, flatter maxima than in AN750-T, consistent with a more uniform carbon distribution after higher-temperature annealing.
The caption labels panel (b) as "Atomic concentration statistics" and titles the group "Quantitative strategy of phases composition".
The citing text states that carbon elements are mainly concentrated in B/TM, FM and RA (Fig. 8(a)).
The citing text states that the data selected along the red dashed lines are shown in Fig. 8(b).
The citing text states that with increasing annealing temperature the distribution of carbon elements becomes more uniform, while the distribution of other elements shows no significant differences.
The citing text states that the average elemental compositions of phases AN750-T, AN800-T and AN850-T are summarised in Table A1 in Appendix A.
